This reg is the audio channel x (x=0,1,2,3) DMA data buffer. | Address | Name | Description |

| Bit | Function |

| 2 | CSYTRUE |
| 1 | VSYTRUE |
| 0 | HSYTRUE |

HARDDIS This bit is used to disable the hardwired vertical horizontal window limits. It is cleared upon reset.

LPENDIS When this bit is a low and LPE ([BPLCON0](#bplcon0), bit 3) is enabled, the light-pen latched value(beam hit position) will be read by [VHPOSR](#vhposr), [VPOSR](#vposr) and [HHPOSR](#hhposw). When the bit is a high the light-pen latched value is ignored and the actual beam counter position is read by [VHPOSR](#vhposr), [VPOSR](#vposr), and [HHPOSR](#hhposw).

VARVBEN Use the comparator generated vertical blank (from [VBSTRT](#vbstrt), [VBSTOP](#vbstrt)) to run the internal chip stuff-sending RGA signals to Denise, starting sprites,resetting light pen. It also disables the hard stop on the vertical display window.

LOLDIS Disable long line/short toggle. This is useful for DUAL mode where even multiples are wanted, or in any single display where this toggling is not desired.

CSCBEN The variable composite sync comes out on the HSY pin, and the variable composite blank comes out on the VSY pin. The idea is to allow all the information to come out of the chip for a DUAL mode display. The normal monitor uses the normal composite sync, and the variable composite sync &blank come out the HSY & VSY pins. The bits VARVSTEN & VARHSYEN (below) have priority over this control bit.

VARVSYEN Comparator VSY -> VSY pin. The variable VSY is set vertically on [VSSTRT](#vsstrt), reset vertically on [VSSTOP](#vtotal), with the horizontal position for set set & reset [HSSTRT](#hsstrt) on short fields (all fields are short if LACE = 0) and [HCENTER](#hcenter) on long fields (every other field if LACE = 1).

VARHSYEN Comparator HSY -> HSY pin. Set on [HSSTRT](#hsstrt) value, reset on [HSSTOP](#hsstrt) value.

VARBEAMEN Enables the variable beam counter comparators to operate (allowing different beam counter total values) on the main horiz counter. It also disables hard display stops on both horizontal and vertical.

DUAL Run the horizontal comparators with the alternate horizontal beam counter, and starts the UHRES pointer chain with the reset of this counter rather than the normal one. This allows the UHRES pointers to come out more than once in a horizontal line, assuming there is some memory bandwidth left (it doesn't work in 640*400*4 interlace mode) also, to keep the two displays synced, the horizontal line lengths should be multiples of each other. If you are amazingly clever, you might not need to do this.

PAL Set appropriate decodes (in normal mode) for PAL. In variable beam counter mode this bit disables the long line/short line toggle- ends up short line.

VARCSYEN Enables CSY from the variable decoders to come out the CSY (VARCSY is set on [HSSTRT](#hsstrt) match always, and also on [HCENTER](#hcenter) match when in vertical sync. It is reset on [HSSTOP](#hsstop) match when VSY and on both [HBSTRT](#hbstrt) & [HBSTOP](#hbstrt) matches during VSY. A reasonable composite can be generated by setting [HCENTER](#hcenter) half a horizontal line from [HSSTRT](#hsstrt), and [HBSTOP](#hbstrt) at ([HSSTOP](#hsstop)-[HSSTRT](#hsstrt)) before [HCENTER](#hcenter), with [HBSTRT](#hbstrt) at ( [HSSTOP](#hsstop)-[HSSTRT](#hsstrt)) before [HSSTRT](#hsstrt).

HSYTRUE, VSYTRUE, CSYTRUE These change the polarity of the HSY*, VSY*, & CSY* pins to HSY, VSY, & CSY respectively for input and output.

Since they have separate modulos, the odd and even bit planes may have sizes that are different from each other, as well as different from the display window size.

If scan-doubling is enabled, BPL1MOD serves as the primary bitplane modulos and BPL2MOD serves as the alternate. Lines whose LSBs of beam counter and DIWSTRT match are designated primary, whereas lines whose LSBs don't match are designated alternate.

The coprocessor is basically a 2 cycle machine that requests the bus only during odd memory cycles. (4 memory cycles per in)

It has priority over the blitter and microprocessor.

There are only three types of instructions, MOVE immediate, WAIT UNTIL, and SKIP IF. All instructions require 2 bus cycles (and two instruction words). Since only the odd bus cycles are requested, 4 memory cycle times are required per instruction. (memory cycles are 280 ns).

There are two indirect jump registers COP1LC and COP2LC. These are 20 bit pointer registers whose contents are used to modify program counter for initialization or jumps.

They are transfered to the program counter whenever strobe address COPJMP1 or COPJMP2 are written. In addition COP1LC is automatically used at the beginning of each vertical blank time.

It is important that one of the jump registers be initialized and its jump strobe address hit, after power up but before coprocessor DMA is initialized. This insures a determined startup address, and state.

The lores bitplane fetch period is 8 CCKs in order: 8, 4, 6, 2, 7, 3, 5, 1 (7 and 8 are unused on OCS). Two lores pixels are output per CCK. One word (16-bits) fetched per CCK, so 16 pixels fetched for each bitplane each period\n"

The hires bitplane fetch period is also 8 CCKs during which each bitplane is fetched twice: 4, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 3, 1 Four hires pixels are output per CCK. One word (16-bits) fetched per CCK, so 32 pixels fetched for each bitplane each period\n"

The DMA cycle values encoded are the adjusted values from the Hardware Reference Manual Figure 6-11 Time Slot Allocation. The true DMA slot value = (DDFSTOP/DDFSTART value & mask) + 4 where mask is $FC for OCS and $FE for ECS/AGA and +4 to undo Hardware Reference Manual timing slot diagram adjustment.

DDFSTRT encodes the first bitplane fetch period start DMA slot. This is the first DMA cycle at which a complete bitplane fetch period (up to 8 lores bitplanes) will commence. First bitplane fetch period start DMA slot = (DDFSTRT & mask) + 4 For example: for "normal" DDFSTRT 0038, First bitplane fetch period start = ($38 & FC) + 4 = 3C CCK (OCS) Fetches start at DDFSTRT, no matter what.

DDFSTOP encodes the final bitplane fetch period start DMA slot. This is the final DMA cycle at which a complete bitplane fetch period (up to 8 lores bitplanes) will commence. Final bitplane fetch period start DMA slot = (DDFSTOP) & mask) + 4 For example: for "normal" DDFSTOP 00D0, final bitplane fetch period start = ($D0 & FC) + 4 = D4 CCK (OCS). The final DMA fetch slot is DB (BPL1DAT is fetched last) Hardware data fetch stop to prevent bitplane data fetch overlapping memory refresh or disk DMA cycles: Final bitplane fetch period start slot is clamped to $D8 + 4 The fetch stopping condition is evaulated when a bitplane fetch period (8 CCKs) completes. When DDFSTOP matches, one final period (8 CCKs) of bitplane data is fetched.
